transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm just... I'm just so worn out. That's really what brought me in. It's like, even just walking from the bedroom to the kitchen feels like I've been hauling lumber all day. And it doesn't matter how much I sit down or try to rest, it just doesn't give me anything back. I'm just exhausted all the time.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah, I have. I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling right in my chest. And some days... well, I just go sit out in the garage and cry. I don't even know what starts it, honestly. But yeah, I've been feeling really down.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I used to look forward to a lot of things... going to choir, playing pickup ball, working on cars. I always liked grilling for the family, too. But now, I just can't make myself care enough to do any of it. I don't show up anymore, and I don't even answer people's texts when they reach out. I just don't have it in me.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about four months now. It started right around the time my wife went back to working full-time. Since she did that, I've been spending most of the weekdays just alone at the house, and... yeah, that's about when all this really set in.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you were dead?

Yeah. The thought just keeps coming up that I should just be dead. And... well, when I'm alone here at the house, it scares me, because I start thinking I might actually do something to make that happen.
Have you noticed any changes in your movement or activity level, such as feeling restless or having trouble sitting still?

No, it's actually the opposite of being restless. Everything I do has just... slowed way down. It feels like my body is moving through mud all the time. Even talking is hard. When someone asks me a question, I can hear them fine, but... it just takes me a really long time to actually get the words out to answer them.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight recently?
No, I haven't really noticed any change in my weight. I haven't been checking or anything, but my clothes still fit about the same.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

Yeah, I do. I just... I keep thinking about how I've failed my wife, and my kids. My church, too. Honestly, it feels like... well, like every bad thing happening around us right now is somehow a punishment. Like it's all happening to punish me for not being the man I was supposed to be.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about anything lately?
No, not really anxious. I'm not... worried about the future or anything like that. I just feel heavy and guilty, like I said. But I wouldn't call it anxiety.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating or making decisions?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any trouble with my concentration. And... well, I don't have a lot of big decisions to make these days anyway, but the ones I do make seem fine. I can focus on things alright when I need to.
Have you had any periods in the last four months where you felt somewhat better for a few days?

No, I haven't. It's just been... the same. Every day feels just as heavy as the last. I haven't had any days where I felt better or things seemed lighter. It's just been a constant weight for months now.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms were so severe that you couldn't get out of bed?

No, not really. I mean, it's hard to get up sometimes because I just don't see the point, but I haven't been completely stuck in bed. I eventually get up, even if it takes a while. I just don't do much once I am up.
Have you been feeling fidgety or having trouble sitting still?

No, I haven't been fidgety. It's actually the opposite. Everything I do has slowed way down. It feels like my body is moving through mud. And... even when people ask me something, I can hear the question just fine, but it takes me a really long time to actually get the words out to answer them. Everything just takes so much effort.
Would you say your low mood and other symptoms are consistently worse in the morning or are they fairly consistent throughout the day?
It's pretty much the same all day. I haven't really noticed it being worse in the morning or anything like that. It's just a constant feeling from the time I wake up until I go to sleep.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in, even if it's just a little bit?

No, not really. I used to look forward to things. I sang in a choir, played pickup basketball, liked working on cars... I used to grill out for the family all the time. But now... I just can't make myself care enough to do any of it. I don't show up to things anymore, and I don't even answer people's texts when they ask where I am. There's just no pleasure in any of it now.
Have you been feeling like you're fidgeting or having an inability to sit still when you're alone or with others?

No, like I mentioned a few minutes ago, I haven't been fidgety at all. It's really the exact opposite. Whether I'm by myself or if someone else is around, I don't have any urge to move around or anything. I mostly just sit there.
Would you say your symptoms have been severe enough to interfere with your ability to work or take care of daily responsibilities?

Yeah, they really have. I mean, I can't even manage the house anymore. I had all these handyman plans—projects I was supposed to get done around the place—and I just can't follow through on any of it. It's... it's gotten bad enough that my wife is actually scared to leave me alone right now. I just... I don't trust myself when the thoughts get bad, so she feels like she has to stay close by.
Do you notice any difference in how you feel at different times of the day?
Not really, no. It just feels the same all the time. Morning, night... it doesn't seem to make a difference. It's just a constant heavy feeling that doesn't let up.
